habitat: 간석지, 염전, 논, 하구 삼각주, 습지의 풀밭
summary: 봄과 가을에 국내를 흔하게 지나가는 나그네새로, 갯벌·염전·논·하구 삼각주와 습지 풀밭에서 지낸다. 무리를 지어 다니며 게를 비롯한 갑각류를 주로 먹는다. 유라시아 대륙 북부에서 번식해 알 4개를 낳고, 인도·동남아시아·호주에서 겨울을 난다.

art.subject: Terek Sandpiper (Xenus cinereus), adult in breeding plumage, as seen on Korean tidal flats during spring migration (late April–May): head, neck and upperparts pale brownish-grey with fine dark shaft streaks; a bold blackish line along each side of the back formed by the black centres of the upper scapulars; faint whitish supercilium in front of the eye; neck sides and upper breast washed grey-brown with fine dark streaks; rest of the underparts clean white. Bill long and black with a dull yellowish-orange base. Dark eye with no eye-ring. Short orange-yellow legs.
art.pose: foraging on wet mud in a loose flock, chasing a small crab
art.scene: Korean tidal mudflat near an estuary during spring migration, wet mud and shallow channels; no people, buildings or text
views: adult breeding (spring), side view standing on mud: long upturned black bill with yellowish base, pale grey-brown upperparts finely streaked black with a black line along the scapulars, grey-brown streaked breast sides, white underparts, short orange-yellow legs
adult, head detail in profile: long bill upturned along its whole length with a yellowish base, faint whitish supercilium, fine grey-brown streaks on the neck and upper breast
adult in flight seen from above, head, body and tail in one line: grey upperwing with a broad white trailing edge on the secondaries, plain grey rump and tail without any white
art.build: Medium-small sandpiper, 23cm, clearly larger than a Dunlin and much smaller than a feral pigeon; low-slung, horizontal carriage with a slightly front-heavy look. Bill long, clearly longer than the head, fairly slender and upturned along its whole length, not only at the tip. Legs strikingly short for the bird's size, orange-yellow. At rest the wingtips reach about the tail tip. Tail short, plain grey. In flight grey upperwing with a broad white trailing edge to the secondaries, and plain grey rump and tail with no white on the back. Feeds with fast, darting runs, often bobbing its rear like a Common Sandpiper.
avoid: Do not paint long legs; the Terek's legs are short, unlike Common Greenshank or Marsh Sandpiper which share its grey look.
Do not paint a white rump or a white wedge up the back (Common Greenshank, Spotted Redshank).
Do not paint red legs (Common Redshank) or dark legs; they are orange-yellow.
Do not paint a straight or downcurved bill; it is upturned from the base, though far less sharply than an avocet's.
